Issued at 300 AM EDT Thu Aug 6 2026

Today-Tonight... Upper level high pressure off the eastern US coast 
will remain in place through the period as a trough moves eastward 
across the Midwest. At the surface, high pressure just off the 
eastern US in the western Atlantic will move ever so slightly 
northward into tonight. Locally winds will become more easterly 
areawide, with speeds generally 5-10 mph. This dominate onshore flow 
will continue to promote isolated onshore-moving showers along the 
coast through the morning and early afternoon hours. Can not rule 
out an isolated lightning storm or two moving onshore through that 
time. Coverage of showers and lightning storms will increase and 
transition to across the interior in the afternoon as the diffuse 
east coast sea breeze moves inland. Moisture across the area will 
remain high, with forecast PW values of 1.9-2.1" across the area, 
which supports convection into this afternoon. There is a medium to 
high (40-70 percent) chance of rain and lightning storms this 
afternoon. Due to the persistent east to southeast flow aloft, 
convection today will move west to northwest around 10-15 mph.
 
The environment is conducive for storms this afternoon, with 
forecast soundings showing plenty of instability (MUCAPE 2200-3000 
J/kg), Strong buoyancy (lifted index greater than -4), cooler 
temperatures aloft (-8C to -9C at 500 mb), and ample downdraft 
potential (DCAPE 500-800 J/kg). Because of this, the main storm 
hazards today will be frequent lightning, gusty winds of 50 mph, 
small hail, and locally heavy rainfall. Due to the potential for 
multiple rounds of showers and storms, the threat for minor, 
localized flooding will continue. Any lingering activity will 
diminish late this evening, with mostly dry conditions overnight. 
However, isolated to scattered showers and storms will continue to 
be possible across the Atlantic waters overnight, with some of this 
activity potentially moving onshore along the coast. 

Temperatures will be near normal for this time of year with 
afternoon highs in the upper 80s to low 90s. These temperatures 
combined with humidity will produce peak heat indices of 100-105F 
this afternoon. Conditions will continue to be muggy into tonight,
with overnight lows in the low to mid 70s. 

Friday-Sunday... An upper level high pressure in the western 
Atlantic on Friday will steadily shift southward and build across 
the Florida peninsula by late weekend. At the surface, an inverted 
trough over the Bahamas on Friday will lift northward across the 
Florida peninsula through early weekend. Locally, this inverted 
trough will bring an increase in moisture across the area, with 
forecast PW values of 2.0-2.2" areawide. This will result in above 
normal rain chances through early weekend. There is a high (70-80 
percent) chance of rain and lightning storms on Friday, and a medium 
to high (50-70 percent) chance on Saturday. Rain and storm chances 
are forecast to return closer to normal on Sunday (PoP 30-60 
percent) as winds become lighter locally as the ridge axis moves over 
the Florida peninsula, resulting in a more diurnal pattern. Early 
morning showers across the local waters and along the coast each day 
will spread inland through the late morning and afternoon hours in 
the southeast to east flow. The environment supports convection with 
forecast soundings showing plenty of instability (MUCAPE 2000-2600 
J/kg), cooler temperatures aloft (-7 C to -8 C at 500 mb), and 
sufficient downdraft potential (DCAPE 600-900 J/kg). Because of this, 
the main storm hazards will be frequent lightning strikes, gusty 
winds of 50 mph, and locally heavy rainfall. Multiple rounds of 
showers will increase the potential for localized minor flooding in 
some spots. Any lingering activity will diminish by late evening. 

Seasonable temperatures are forecast each day, especially late week 
through early weekend, as the increased moisture across the area 
will result in higher cloud cover. This will limit daytime heating 
across the area. Afternoon highs will be in the low 90s Friday and 
Saturday, with low to mid 90s forecast on Sunday as a little more 
daytime heating is anticipated to occur. These temperatures combined 
with humidity will produce peak heat index values of 100-105F Friday 
and Saturday, and 102-107F on Sunday.

Florida peninsula through the period as the high pressure slowly 
shifts eastward from the western Atlantic on Monday into the Gulf 
and the Deep South by mid week. At the surface, high pressure across 
the western Atlantic will slowly shift southward into mid week, with
